newsitem.title: GERMANY: German advertisers lambast Vatican criticism.
newsitem.headline: German advertisers lambast Vatican criticism.

text.p: The German Advertising Association (ZAW) on Tuesday slammed a Vatican report which had condemned advertising as a modern force of evil and accused the industry of failing in its ethical duty.
The ZAW said in its report "Advertising. And Morals" that advertisers did not have the influence the Vatican claimed, and actually helped people to make more informed decisions.

The organisation said it objected to the Vatican's portrayal of consumers as "victims" of advertising, saying it presented an authoritarian image of society which did not fit democratic market economies.

"Citizens, at least in a modern society, are competent, sovereign and autonomous in their decisions. This creates growing conflict with what used to be all-powerful influences like political parties, churches and unions," said the ZAW.

The Vatican Pontifical Council for Social Communications released a report entitled "Ethics in Advertising" last month urging advertisers to stop pandering to lust, envy and greed and show more morality in their work.

The association did agree with the Vatican that advertising should not lie, harm "human worth or the common good", or present religious images disrespectfully. It noted that the church had also stressed the economic benefits of advertising.
"Advertising helps to finance the media, including church publications, and to provide people all over the world with information, entertainment and inspiration," the ZAW said.
